text: The sunny boulevard from the very first day is unrecognizable.
No people. No traffic. No light.
By now, the average temperature on Earth would be around minus seventeen degrees. Colder than most of us have ever felt.
The oceans are beginning to freeze from the surface.
Salt water only freezes at around minus two degrees, so the sea holds out longer than the land. But not forever.
Along the shore, a thin skin of ice grows a little thicker every hour.
Most people are no longer outside.
They have gathered wherever there is still heat. Fuel. Firewood. A generator.
This car has not moved in days. Its roof is covered in frost, as hard as stone.
Every breath hangs in the air like smoke.
